claims.text: Replacing Mn with Si or Al in CrFeCoNiX alloys promotes formation of a stable protective oxide above 900 °C.
The resulting protective oxide is coherent and slow-growing in oxidizing or corrosive atmospheres.
The beneficial effect of replacing Mn with Si or Al operates through a reactive-element effect at oxide-scale grain boundaries.
Si- or Al-containing alloys form a thin, continuous surface oxide enriched in SiO2 or Al2O3.
Si or Al segregates to oxide grain boundaries.
Segregation of Si or Al to oxide grain boundaries reduces intergranular diffusion during oxide growth.
Segregation of Si or Al to oxide grain boundaries reduces thermal strain during oxide growth.
Reduced intergranular diffusion and thermal strain inhibit defect formation in the oxide scale.
Inhibition of oxide-scale defect formation mitigates crack initiation and spallation.
Mitigation of cracking and spallation stabilizes the protective oxide scale.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, Si- or Al-containing alloys will have lower oxide-scale growth rates than CrFeCoNiMn.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, Si- or Al-containing alloys will exhibit less oxide cracking and spallation than CrFeCoNiMn.
Under identical high-temperature conditions, Si- or Al-containing alloys will exhibit greater oxide-scale adhesion than CrFeCoNiMn.
The proposed behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid-solution states.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C in typical oxidizing or corrosive service atmospheres.
